page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ads_v7 is a constrained-vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, delivering 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core. The architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware resource allocation is heavily skewed toward memory and storage density. The system provides 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding 32.0 GB per vCPU, paired with 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. There are no discrete GPUs allocated, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. In benchmark tests, the AMD EPYC core achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution (3779.98) as well as compression metrics such as gzip single-threaded (41.23 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (18.42 GB/sec). Multi-core benchmarks reflect the 8 vCPU footprint, registering average tier performance in stress-ng multi-core (15115.85) and PassMark CPU (18926.2).

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate 919.29 GB/sec for small cached blocks, tapering to 49.32 GB/sec for uncached read-only and 33.98 GB/sec for uncached write operations. In workload-oriented testing, Redis operations achieve 14.91 million operations per second, static web serving reaches 15.87 GB/sec, and LLM text generation on a 135M parameter model registers a strong 318.76 tokens per second. Performance dips to the lower tier when processing prompts for larger 7B models (31.4 tokens per second).

By constraining the core count to 8 vCPUs on a chassis containing 256.0 GB of RAM and fast NVMe storage, the E32-8ads_v7 offers significant cost efficiency for software licensed on a per-core basis. It is tailored for memory-bound applications that do not require massive parallel compute threads, including large in-memory caching layers, relational databases, and local I/O intensive analytical workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor offering 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores) clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Built with a 1:32 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 256.0 GB of RAM and 1888 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, without discrete GPUs. Benchmark results emphasize top-tier single-core and compression performance, complemented by 14.91 million Redis operations per second and 919.29 GB/sec cached memory read throughput. Constraining the compute count while preserving massive RAM capacity and high-performance local storage makes this instance particularly well-suited for cost-effective memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, memory-bound caching systems, and per-core licensed database software.
